channel.title: The Example Garden Notes
channel.description: Short, practical notes for a small vegetable garden. A fixture feed invented for this guide's lab.

item.title: Watering tomatoes without drowning them
item.description: Tomatoes like a deep drink twice a week, not a shallow sip every day. Water at the base of the plant, early in the morning, and keep the leaves dry. A layer of mulch — straw, shredded leaves, or grass clippings — slows the soil drying out between waterings.

item.title: Compost: the three-bin habit
item.description: One bin filling, one bin cooking, one bin ready to use. Keep the mix near three parts dry material to one part green, turn it when you walk past with a fork in your hand, and let rain do most of the watering.

item.title: Why seedlings lean toward the window
item.description: Seedlings grow toward light, so a tray on a windowsill leans within days. Turn the tray a quarter turn every morning, or give the plants light from directly above, and the stems stay short and sturdy instead of long and pale.

item.title: A five-minute soil test with a jam jar
item.description: Fill a jar one third with soil, top up with water, shake hard, and let it settle for a day. Sand sinks first, silt settles next, clay stays cloudy longest. The layers tell you roughly what you are gardening in, and what to add.

item.title: Feeding the soil in autumn
item.description: When the beds empty in autumn, cover them. A blanket of compost or leaf mould protects the surface from winter rain, feeds the worms, and saves you a digging job in spring.

item.title: Herbs that forgive beginners
item.description: Mint, chives and parsley put up with a great deal of neglect. Give mint a pot of its own — it spreads without asking — and cut chives hard whenever the clump looks tired; both come back as if nothing happened.

item.title: Reading a seed packet properly
item.description: The back of a seed packet answers four questions: when to sow, how deep, how far apart, and when to expect the harvest. The date stamp matters too — old seed still grows, but fewer seeds in each packet will.

item.title: The case for a small garden
item.description: A garden you can weed in twenty minutes is a garden that gets weeded. Start with one bed, learn what the soil and the season do in your patch, and let next year's garden be the bigger one.
